name: Sacrifice and Atonement (The Lamb of God)

objectives.text: Identify Jesus as the one John the Baptist called the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world
Retell how Jesus said that as the Good Shepherd he would lay down his life for his sheep
Retell how God made garments of skin to clothe Adam and Eve after they sinned
Explain from Scripture that sin separates people from God and deserves his judgment
Retell the account of Abraham and Isaac and identify the ram God provided in Isaac's place
Describe the animal sacrifices offered by Abel and Noah in the early chapters of Genesis
Retell the first Passover and explain why the blood on the doorposts spared the Israelite households
Define atonement as God's provision for covering sin and reconciling sinners to himself
Explain from Leviticus and Hebrews why the shedding of blood was required for atonement under the law
Compare the Passover lamb with Jesus as the unblemished lamb whose blood redeems his people
Describe the main Levitical offerings and the purpose Scripture gives for each
Explain the roles of the two goats on the Day of Atonement and what each pictured about the removal of sin
Explain how the Lord's Supper proclaims Christ's once-for-all sacrifice as the Reformed tradition confesses it
Explain substitution as Christ bearing the curse and penalty of sin in the place of sinners
Analyze how Isaiah 53 presents the Suffering Servant as a substitute who bears the sins of others
Compare the repeated Levitical sacrifices with Christ's once-for-all sacrifice as Hebrews 10 presents them
Explain how the New Testament describes believers offering themselves as living sacrifices and sacrifices of praise in response to Christ's atonement
Distinguish the biblical terms propitiation, expiation, reconciliation, and redemption as aspects of Christ's atoning work
Analyze how Paul presents the cross as showing God to be both just and the justifier of those who have faith in Jesus
Trace the Lamb theme from the Old Testament to Revelation and explain how each passage develops it
Evaluate why animal sacrifices could not take away sin yet were ordained by God as types pointing to Christ
Evaluate moral influence, governmental, and Christus Victor accounts of the atonement against the Reformed confession of penal substitution using Scripture
Analyze the passages the Reformed tradition uses to teach definite atonement and explain how its confessions state the doctrine
Create a written or visual synthesis tracing the theme of sacrifice from Eden to the worship of the Lamb in the new creation

changes: Dropped the filler K objective (identify a lamb) and replaced it with identifying Jesus as the Lamb of God. Rewrote vague items: 'recall that sin needs forgiveness' now explains sin's separation and judgment, and 'observe that blood was used' became an explanation of Leviticus 17:11 with Hebrews 9:22. Kept and reworded Abraham and Isaac, the definition of atonement, the Passover comparison, the scapegoat (expanded to both Day of Atonement goats), substitution, Leviticus and Hebrews 10, propitiation (broadened to distinguish the related atonement terms), the Lamb study (now a tracing objective), the inadequacy of animal sacrifices, penal substitution (now evaluated against alternative views), and the Eden to Heaven synthesis. Dropped the tearing of the Temple curtain, which is left to The Temple and the Presence of God sibling. Added objectives on Genesis 3:21, John 10, the sacrifices of Abel and Noah, the first Passover, the Levitical offerings, the Lord's Supper, Isaiah 53, living sacrifices, Romans 3:21-26, and definite atonement. Corrected confession citations to articles that state each doctrine (WCF 7.5, 8.4, 8.5, 8.8, 11.3, 29.2, WSC Q19, Q25, Q84, Q96, HC Q37, Q40, Q75, Canons of Dort 2.8).
